messages.author: 6e3bf202055f2791
messages.subject: exogenous variables
parts:
Dear all, I have a problem with one exogenous variable. I specify the following model:

m <- '
SocPerfState =~ d1 + d2 
EconPerfState =~ k6
PersEconCond =~   g1r + Unempl 
Clientel =~ l1br +  l4r  
Authorit =~ k2_k3_k4r.auth + f3 + k1
Trust.StateInst =~   f3 + f4 
Trust.PolInst =~ f6 + f7 
Violence =~  p2_22cr + p2_22br 
GDvote ~   Clientel + Violence + Trust.StateInst + Trust.PolInst + Authorit +  SocPerfState + EconPerfState+ PersEconCond + female
'

When the exogenous variable "female" is not in the regression, all the fit statistics of the model are really happy. When I add the "female" in the model, then the fit statistics are all over the place e.g.


lavaan (0.5-15) converged normally after 166 iterations

                                                  Used       Total
  Number of observations                          2652        5025

  Estimator                                       DWLS      Robust
  Minimum Function Test Statistic              315.154     405.106
  Degrees of freedom                                84          84
  P-value (Chi-square)                           0.000       0.000
  Scaling correction factor                                  0.817
  Shift parameter                                           19.486
    for simple second-order correction (Mplus variant)


In effect, the regression part predicts voting (yes/no). Female increases the probit R2 from 0.46 to 0.56!!! However, it makes the chi-square terrible (the model fit becomes significant). 
So, should I say that this variable cannot be part of the model because of the chi-square, although it offers 0.10 to my R2? 

And I have a second question. How much trust  should I put to this R2? I udnerstand that this is a probit R2, therefore it is a pseudo-R2. Does lavaan report the MacFadden R2 or is this another type of R2?

Thank you for your time

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: exogenous variables
parts:
On 01/28/2014 08:23 AM, Jason Lamprianou wrote:
> In effect, the regression part predicts voting (yes/no). Female
> increases the probit R2 from 0.46 to 0.56!!! However, it makes the
> chi-square terrible (the model fit becomes significant).

Hm. Hard to say. Would yo be able to send me the data (or a snippet of
the data) + the full R script?

> And I have a second question. How much trust should I put to this R2? I
> udnerstand that this is a probit R2, therefore it is a pseudo-R2.

It is indeed a pseudo-R2, so its use is limited at best. It represents
the explained variance proportion of the underlying continuous latent
response variable (see McKelvey and Zavoina 1975).

Yves.
